description: Search, read, and list comments on Notion pages through Notion's official remote MCP server, signed in with the connected user's own Notion account.

steps: Copy the Callback URL shown below.

POST {"client_name":"Open Connector","redirect_uris":["<Callback URL>"],"grant_types":["authorization_code","refresh_token"],"response_types":["code"],"token_endpoint_auth_method":"none"} as JSON to https://mcp.notion.com/register.
Copy the returned client_id into the Client ID field below and leave Client Secret empty.
Connect with OAuth. Notion MCP is in beta: tool names and result shapes can change without notice, and some search filters need a Business or Enterprise plan.

actions.name: fetch_page
actions.description: Read one Notion page through notion-fetch by ID or URL. Returns the title, properties block, Markdown content, a truncated flag, and the raw response.

id.description: The Notion page ID or URL.
The requested page ID or URL, echoed back.

title.description: The page title, when the server names one.

url.description: The Notion URL of the page, when the server names one.

page_last_edited_at.description: The last-edited time, when the server reports one.

properties.description: The page's properties block as the server rendered it.

truncated.description: Whether the server cut the content short.

raw.description: The untouched text Notion's MCP tool returned, kept beside the typed fields so a changed tool shape can still be read.

outputSchema.description: A Notion page as notion-fetch returned it.

actions.name: get_self
actions.description: Identify the connected Notion user through notion-get-users with user_id self. Returns the user ID, name, and email the server reports.

email.description: The user's email address, when the server reports one.

type.description: The user type, such as person or bot.

user.description: A Notion user as the MCP server reports it. Fields the server omits are absent.

raw.description: The untouched text Notion's MCP tool returned, kept beside the typed fields so a changed tool shape can still be read.

actions.name: list_comments
actions.description: List the comments on one Notion page through notion-get-comments, flattened across discussions. Block-level and resolved discussions are included unless turned off; the server offers no paging.

include_all_blocks.description: Whether to include comments on every block of the page. Defaults to true.

include_resolved.description: Whether to include resolved discussions. Defaults to true.

inputSchema.description: The page whose comments to list.

discussion_id.description: The discussion thread the comment belongs to.

email.description: The user's email address, when the server reports one.

type.description: The user type, such as person or bot.

created_by.description: A Notion user as the MCP server reports it. Fields the server omits are absent.

items.description: One comment. Fields the server omits are absent.

raw.description: The untouched text Notion's MCP tool returned, kept beside the typed fields so a changed tool shape can still be read.

outputSchema.description: Comments on a Notion page, flattened across discussions.

actions.name: search
actions.description: Search Notion pages through notion-search with optional text, sort, page size, date-range and creator filters. Returns typed results, the search type that ran, the server's notices about dropped filters, and the raw response. Filtering by editor or last-edited date and sorting by date need a Business or Enterprise plan; other plans drop them and name them in notices. When the connection can use AI search, a non-empty keyword query with no exact filter and relevance order runs AI search and can return results from connected apps. Notion allows 30 searches a minute.

query.description: Search text. An empty string lists pages by the sort order alone.

sort.description: Result order. The beta server accepted "relevance" (the default), "last_edited" and "created"; the value is passed through as given. Date sorts need a Business or Enterprise plan; other plans fall back to relevance and say so in notices.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results. Notion allows 1 to 50.

max_highlight_length.description: Maximum length of the highlight snippet on each result; 0 turns highlights off.

start_date.description: The earliest day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: The latest day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD.

last_edited_date_range.description: Only pages last edited in this day-precision range. Business and Enterprise plans only; other plans drop the filter and name it in notices.

start_date.description: The earliest day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: The latest day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD.

created_date_range.description: Only pages created in this day-precision range.

created_by_user_ids.description: Only pages created by these Notion user IDs.

edited_by_user_ids.description: Only pages edited by these Notion user IDs. Business and Enterprise plans only; other plans drop the filter and name it in notices.

filters.description: Extra filters passed through under the tool's filters argument as given. The typed filters above take precedence over the same keys here.

type.description: Which search ran, as the server reports it: "workspace_search", or "ai_search" when Notion routed a keyword query to AI search, whose results can come from connected apps such as Slack that fetch_page cannot read.

id.description: The page or data source ID.

url.description: The Notion URL of the result.

type.description: The result type, such as page.

timestamp.description: The last-edited time the server reports for the result.

path.description: The breadcrumb path to the result.

items.description: One search result. Fields the server omits are absent.

notices.description: Server notices as plain text, such as a filter dropped on this plan.

raw.description: The untouched text Notion's MCP tool returned, kept beside the typed fields so a changed tool shape can still be read.

actions.name: tool_access
actions.description: Report each MCP tool's access status on the connected Notion plan through notion-get-tool-access, keyed by the tool's base name such as search, with the parameters the plan restricts and the reason for each, such as the edited-by search filter below the Business plan.

tool.description: The tool's base name as the server keys it, such as search or ai_search: the notion- prefix dropped and hyphens turned into underscores.

status.description: The access status: available, available_with_limit, plan_required, upgrade_required, full_version_required, or not_enabled.

parameter.description: The parameter path, such as filters.title_only.

reason.description: Why the parameter is unavailable, as the server words it. Check it against the value you plan to send: a restriction on several teamspaces still allows one.

restricted_parameters.description: Parameters the plan restricts, independent of the status.

upgrade_url.description: Where a workspace upgrade changes the status.

full_version_url.description: Where to get the full version of Notion MCP when the tool needs it.

landing_page_url.description: The plan landing page Notion routes the user through.

landing_page_action.description: What the landing page offers: start_trial, request_trial, or learn_more.

items.description: Access to one MCP tool on the connected plan.

tools.description: One entry per tool the connection exposes, in the server's order.

raw.description: The untouched text Notion's MCP tool returned, kept beside the typed fields so a changed tool shape can still be read.
